history.dynasty: Rathore (founder Rao Bika / Bikaji, on the orders of Karni Mata)
history.period: Late 15th century (before Bikaner's founding in 1488); legend links the site to Vikram Samvat 1465 (verify)
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: The temple is NOT in Bikaner city - it stands at Kodamdesar village, about 24-30 km southwest of Bikaner on the Jaisalmer highway (NH) in Bikaner district; documented here with the corrected location. Kodamdesar was Rao Bika's ORIGINAL capital site: he founded Kodamdesar and installed the Bhairav idol here (on Karni Mata's orders) before shifting his capital and founding Bikaner city in 1488 AD. The temple is an open-air shrine - the large Bhairav idol sits under the open sky with no roofed sanctum, and local lore says no roof could ever be built over it despite several attempts by kings (verify). The idol is set in a marble-paved court with no formal building; devotees regard it as a particularly potent form of the deity. One legend ties the site to the tragic story of Kodamde from Vikram Samvat 1465 (verify - sourced from a devotional video, treat as folklore). The temple is well-regarded locally (rated ~4.6 across travel platforms) and is a standard stop on Bikaner sightseeing circuits along with Gajner.

name: Kodamdesar Bhairav Temple
town: Kodamdesar (CSV town 'Bikaner' is approximate - the temple is ~24-30 km from Bikaner city at Kodamdesar village, Bikaner district)
town_description: Kodamdesar is a historic village on the Jaisalmer highway, about 24-30 km from Bikaner city. It was Rao Bika's first capital before he founded Bikaner in 1488, and it retains that legacy in the open-air Bhairav shrine. The village sits in desert scrubland near the Gajner area; visitors typically combine the temple with Gajner Palace and the Gajner wildlife sanctuary.
